FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Angers have the chance to at least temporarily move out of Ligue 1’s automatic relegation zone when they host an out-of-form Lens side now one month without a win in any competition.

Match News and Current Form

Angers have fallen to 17th following a three-game Ligue 1 losing sequence and have to go back to mid-September for their last victory, 2-0 at home to Troyes, with their six-match winless league run (D1, L5) including three games at Stade Raymond-Kopa (D1, L2). Only once since 1981 have the Black and Whites been on a longer top-flight streak without scoring than their current one of four matches. Their attack has been an issue beyond this season too, as ahead of this round of fixtures, their 11 home goals in league action this year is the joint-lowest such total in Europe’s top five divisions among all ever-present clubs in 2026.

Few would have expected Lens to be just six points above Angers this deep into the campaign, but they are enduring a turbulent period after a change of head coach this month. The Blood and Gold have lost four of their last five games across all competitions (D1) - the latest of which was a 3-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at RB Leipzig - with two of those encounters occurring under new boss Didier Digard (D1, L1). Lens are now at risk of losing back-to-back Ligue 1 away matches without scoring for the first time since 2014, and they may need to find the net to take any points here as one of three teams yet to keep a clean sheet in France’s top flight this season. 

Head-to-Head History

Lens have won the last seven H2Hs, their longest top-flight winning run ever against a single opponent. 

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Angers have lost 70% of their Ligue 1 games as betting outsiders this season.

Angers have opened the scoring a joint league-low three times in the first 11 matchdays this term (W2, L1).

Lens have won only 37.5% of their Ligue 1 games as favourites this season.

An equal league-high nine of Lens’ first 11 matches this term have seen both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Angers winger Jim Allevinah has faced Lens more times than any other club without ever winning (D3, L3), failing to score or assist in any of those games. This has been an enjoyable match-up recently though for Lens’ Abdallah Sima, who has registered a goal involvement in two of his last three games against Angers, emerging victorious all three times.

Angers seemingly have no fresh absentees following their 4-0 loss to Paris FC, while Lens were without Michaël Cuisance against Leipzig. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Lens’ fairly strong defence and Angers’ inability to score suggests that under 2.5 goals is likely here. 

Author: Aaron Murphy
